chapterFiles.title: Mark 16 — The Resurrection narrative + the longer-ending textual-critical site (Mark 16:9-20 absent in Vaticanus + Sinaiticus)

versionSource: Best-effort reconstruction from earliest-attested Koine Greek uncial codices: Codex Vaticanus (B/03) + Codex Sinaiticus (א/01) + early papyri cross-collation + NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT critical apparatus
sourceCitation: Codex Vaticanus (B/03; Vatican Library Gr. 1209, 4th c. CE) + Codex Sinaiticus (א/01; British Library Add. 43725 et al., 4th c. CE) as primary uncial witnesses. Cross-collation against P45 (Chester Beatty I, ~250 CE) for Mark/Acts; P75 (Bodmer XIV-XV, ~175-225 CE) for Luke; P47 (Chester Beatty III, ~250 CE) for Revelation. Critical apparatus: NA28 (Nestle-Aland 28th, 2012); UBS5 (United Bible Societies 5th, 2014); SBLGNT (SBL 2010); THGNT (Tyndale House 2017). Commentary references vary by book — see per-book documentation.

subtitles.en: Mark 16 — the Resurrection narrative + the longer-ending textual-critical site

descriptions.en: Mark 16 from the earliest substantial Koine Greek manuscript witnesses (Codex Vaticanus + Codex Sinaiticus + cross-collation against P45). The longer-ending Mark 16:9-20 is ABSENT in Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + P45 — the consensus modern critical-text view is that it is a 2nd-century scribal addition appended to harmonize Mark with the other Gospels. The chapter is preserved here per the established WoH-Translation conventions, with the textual-critical dispute documented in the apparatus.
